themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency in Greenpoint
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus 1.2 per week average over prior 8 weeks (+380%), and new tree requests exploded to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 per week average (+2300%, z-score 8.69), suggesting a sudden canopy crisis or disease outbreak affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: New Tree Request complaints: 3 this week vs 0.1 weekly average (z-score 8.69, severity high)
Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 6 this week vs 1.2 weekly average (z-score 5.73, severity high)
Combined signal suggests acute environmental stressor affecting street trees across district
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept about disease, pest infestation, or weather damage affecting Greenpoint/Williamsburg trees this week
Investigate whether recent storms or drought conditions triggered disproportionate tree loss in this CD

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 18 LAST WEEK versus 7.4 per week baseline (+144%, z-score 5.02), coinciding with unsanitary condition complaints rising to 48 (+63%), signaling a potential sanitation collection failure or improper dumping pattern.
evidence: Residential Disposal Complaint: 18 last week vs 7.4 weekly average (+144%, z-score 5.02)
Unsanitary Condition complaints: 48 last week vs 29.5 weekly average (+63%, z-score 4.7)
Two converging signals suggest systemic waste management breakdown affecting multiple addresses
reporting_angles: Verify with NYC Sanitation whether collection routes were disrupted or redirected last week in Greenpoint/Williamsburg
Canvass blocks with high complaint density to document waste accumulation and interview residents on collection frequency

themes_detail.label: Street-Level Disorder Surge
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints spiked to 9 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 2.1 per week average (+324%, z-score 5.42), mobile food vendor complaints hit 10 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 1.0 average (+900%, z-score 5.2), and 'outside building' complaints rose to 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.4 average (+700%), indicating a convergent spike in street commerce and encampment activity.
evidence: Panhandling complaints: 9 two weeks ago vs 2.1 weekly average (+324%, z-score 5.42)
Mobile Food Vendor complaints: 10 two weeks ago vs 1.0 weekly average (+900%, z-score 5.2)
Outside Building complaints: 3 last week vs 0.4 weekly average (+700%, z-score 5.42)
CB budget requests repeatedly cite 'services for the homeless' (unsolved multi-year issue)
reporting_angles: Interview unhoused individuals and outreach workers about what triggered visible encampment growth 2 weeks ago
Document relationship between informal street vending and commercial/residential displacement pressure in Greenpoint/Williamsburg

themes_detail.label: House of Worship Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: House of worship noise complaints surged to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.2 per week average (+1100%, z-score 6.35), suggesting a new venue opening, event series, or amplified activity affecting adjacent residential blocks.
evidence: House of Worship noise complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly average (z-score 6.35, severity high)
Spike is localized to single issue type, not broad noise elevation
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaint addresses with recent religious institution permits or events filed two weeks ago
Interview community board or residents adjacent to flagged addresses about recent amplified activity or new services

themes_detail.label: Building Alteration Surge
themes_detail.summary: DOB alteration filings total 743 over last 90 days (57% of all 1,299 permits filed), with 20 Berry Street and 200/289 Kent Avenue rezoning applications in active public review, indicating sustained real estate development pressure that may be displacing residents or triggering community concern.
evidence: 743 alteration permits filed in last 90 days (57% of all filings)
5 active ULURP/rezoning applications in pipeline: 200 Kent, 20 Berry, 289 Kent, Monitor Point, 639 Grand Street
CB budget repeatedly requests 'land use planning, technical and urban design support' (unsolved multi-year issue)
reporting_angles: Map alteration permits against rezoning applications to identify which projects are already breaking ground before public approval
Interview long-term residents or small business owners on whether recent alterations are converting ground-floor retail or displacing tenants
